title: The Front-Loaded Mortgage Shock

beats.say: You just bought a $400,000 home with a 30-year mortgage at 6.5%.
beats.visual: A sleek modern house key resting on a dark wood table under warm pendant light, macro shot.

beats.say: It feels like a milestone. But wait until you see where your first payments actually go.
beats.visual: A black fountain pen resting beside a heavy closed ledger, moody side lighting.

beats.say: Over the first 5 years, you will hand over roughly $150,000 in total monthly payments.
beats.visual: A stack of hundred-dollar bills tied with a paper band, low key studio lighting.

beats.say: You assume that money builds equity. You assume you own a chunk of your house now.
beats.visual: A modern architectural model of a house casting a long shadow across a concrete desk.

beats.say: Here's the part nobody mentions. Out of that $150,000, most of it vanishes.
beats.visual: A close-up of a vintage brass desk clock ticking softly in a dimly lit room.

beats.say: After 5 full years of payments, your actual principal balance has barely moved.
beats.visual: A person's hand in a dark sleeve sliding a heavy metal calculator across a dark desk.

beats.say: You have paid down just $17,000 of the original $400,000 balance.
beats.visual: A minimalist white ceramic cup of black coffee steaming faintly in a shaft of morning light.

beats.say: Where did the remaining $133,000 go? Straight to bank interest.
beats.visual: A sleek brass doorknob reflecting a dark hallway, cinematic depth of field.

beats.say: Banks front-load mortgages so they collect their profit before you build any real ownership.
beats.visual: An hourglass with fine black sand pouring rapidly through the narrow glass neck.

beats.say: That is the hidden cost of traditional financing that most buyers completely ignore.
beats.visual: A closed heavy wooden front door viewed from the inside with light creeping underneath.

beats.say: Now you know how the system works. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person walking down a quiet hallway toward a warm light source.

caption: Most homeowners have no idea where their early payments actually go. #mortgage #moneytips #personalfinance #housingmarket #debtfree
description: Analyzing a $400,000 mortgage at 6.5% reveals the brutal reality of front-loaded interest payments over the first five years.
first_comment: Did you know your principal paydown was this low in the first five years?

facts.basis: Standard amortization math for a 30-year fixed loan at 6.5% interest

facts.claim: First 5 years payments total roughly $150,000 with only $17,000 to principal
facts.basis: Standard amortization schedule for a $400k loan at 6.5% results in ~$2,530/month payment where early months are mostly interest
